headline: Saima Wazed Putul resigns as WHO regional head amid fraud allegations
summary: The daughter of ousted PM Sheikh Hasina steps down from her role as Southeast Asia Director after investigations into financial fraud and credentials.
details: Saima Wazed Putul, the WHO's Southeast Asia regional director, has resigned following fraud investigations by the UN agency and Bangladeshi authorities.
The WHO accused Putul of committing financial fraud related to her travel to China and misrepresenting her academic credentials.
Additionally, the agency alleged she illegally acquired a plot of land in Bangladesh, which Putul claims was granted under a law covering the families of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.
Putul had been on unpaid administrative leave since late last year, following charges of fraud and forgery filed by Bangladesh's Anti-Corruption Commission.
In her resignation letter, Putul denied the allegations, attributing the travel fraud to an administrative oversight involving $901 and clarifying her honorary doctorate.
She stated she had lost trust in the WHO leadership and that her financial situation became untenable after nearly a year without pay.
The WHO is expected to announce nominations for the role on October 12, with elections scheduled for January 24.
caption:
Saima Wazed Putul has resigned as the WHO's Southeast Asia head following fraud and forgery investigations.

Saima Wazed Putul, the WHO's Southeast Asia regional director, has resigned following fraud investigations by the UN agency and Bangladeshi authorities.

The WHO accused Putul of committing financial fraud related to her travel to China and misrepresenting her academic credentials.

Additionally, the agency alleged she illegally acquired a plot of land in Bangladesh, which Putul claims was granted under a law covering the families of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.

Putul had been on unpaid administrative leave since late last year, following charges of fraud and forgery filed by Bangladesh's Anti-Corruption Commission.

In her resignation letter, Putul denied the allegations, attributing the travel fraud to an administrative oversight involving $901 and clarifying her honorary doctorate.

She stated she had lost trust in the WHO leadership and that her financial situation became untenable after nearly a year without pay.

The WHO is expected to announce nominations for the role on October 12, with elections scheduled for January 24.

headline_marked: Bhola: [[Two missing after geo-bags collapse]] on Meghna riverbank
headline: Bhola: Two missing after geo-bags collapse on Meghna riverbank
summary: Five people were swept into the river when a section of erosion-control bags suddenly gave way on Wednesday night.
details: Two men, identified as Rakib and Amzad, went missing after a section of geo-bags installed along an erosion-prone stretch of the Meghna river collapsed in Bhola Sadar upazila.

The incident occurred around 7:30pm on Wednesday in the Shibpur area. Five people were sitting and talking on the bags when the structure suddenly gave way due to river erosion, sending them all into the water.
Three survivors, Abdullah, Sagar, and Fahim, managed to swim to safety. Abdullah and Sagar were subsequently taken to a hospital for medical treatment.
One of the missing men, Amzad, is reported to be a member of the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) who had recently returned home on a two-month leave.
Coast Guard personnel and divers launched a rescue operation to locate the missing men. However, the initial search failed to find them.
The rescue operation was suspended shortly before midnight and is scheduled to resume on Thursday morning.
caption:
Five people were swept into the Meghna river after erosion-control geo-bags suddenly collapsed. Two remain missing.

Two men, identified as Rakib and Amzad, went missing after a section of geo-bags installed along an erosion-prone stretch of the Meghna river collapsed in Bhola Sadar upazila.

The incident occurred around 7:30pm on Wednesday in the Shibpur area. Five people were sitting and talking on the bags when the structure suddenly gave way due to river erosion, sending them all into the water.

Three survivors, Abdullah, Sagar, and Fahim, managed to swim to safety. Abdullah and Sagar were subsequently taken to a hospital for medical treatment.

One of the missing men, Amzad, is reported to be a member of the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) who had recently returned home on a two-month leave.

Coast Guard personnel and divers launched a rescue operation to locate the missing men. However, the initial search failed to find them.

The rescue operation was suspended shortly before midnight and is scheduled to resume on Thursday morning.
